source_notes.finding: Bootstrap passes two host References ($0 rpc, $1 log) into evalClosure; guest code only sees external_* closures over them. Arguments and results cross as JSON strings, and rpc uses apply with result.promise so calls overlap.
New ivm.Isolate with memoryLimit per run, disposed in finally. Two timeout layers: the eval timeout stops sync loops, a host timer disposes the isolate while it awaits.
The constructor throws unless Node runs with --no-node-snapshot, because isolate creation otherwise crashes the process. TypeScript is stripped on the host with esbuild, a native binary.

Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment.

Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead.

Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge.
Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript.

The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack.

Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body.

surprises: One of ten default P7 runs ended with the host process segfaulting (exit 139) right after Mastra returned the memory-limit error; the other nine continued normally.
error.line is in the result type but never filled.
